reason: 'The strawberry tasted plain, like nothing at all!' ... 'The sweet taste came back.' Holding your nose makes flavor weaker, not gone; sweetness is sensed by the tongue and is still tasted with the nose held.
'She found it near the A, at the very start of the alphabet. "There you are, B!... You are first."' A is the first letter of the alphabet; B is second.
'The next day, tiny green leaves came up.' Tomato and carrot seeds take about a week or more to sprout, not one day.
'One little sentence had started three games.' Stella's sentence started one game (doctor); Mia started the pirate game, so the count is wrong.
'Next Willow found a soft toy bear. She put it in the animal pile... Now every pile had the same kind of thing.' A toy bear is a toy, not an animal, so it belongs in the toy pile.
'Yes. Today is tomorrow now.' Today is not tomorrow; the day that was called tomorrow yesterday is now called today.
The story never says 'itadakimasu' is said in Japan or that it gives thanks for the food; Grandpa only calls it 'the true word for before we eat.'
'On the third day, Jordan saw something small and green. A sprout!' Carrot seeds usually take one to three weeks to sprout, and they are sown shallow, not in a deep hole.
'He is the umpire,' said Coach. 'The umpire makes sure everyone follows the rules.' The game is soccer (kicking the ball into a net), and the official in soccer is called a referee, not an umpire.
The fact 'Yesterday is the day before today' is never stated; the story only says 'Yesterday already went by.'
'Mom sat in front. Baby Max sat next to Mom in his little seat.' Babies must ride in a car seat in the back seat, never in the front seat.
'But now the yellow pot was all blue inside.' Stirring a blue brush into yellow paint turns the yellow pot green, not blue.
'A big plane went up, up, up into the sky! The plane made wind. The wind pushed a hat right off a man's head.' A plane taking off from the runway does not blow hats off people in the airport.
'Her blocks on the floor bounced a little with each clap.' Clapping hands does not make blocks on the floor bounce.
'Axel counted his beans again. "Four, five, six, seven. Seven!"' He had four beans and got two more, so he has six, not seven.

'It said ducks like bread crumbs.' The park sign endorses feeding ducks bread and the story presents it as good; bread is unhealthy for ducks and parks commonly post signs asking people not to feed them bread.

'You skipped three, Riley,' said Grandma, but Riley's count as written says every word one to ten in order; the real error with nine eggs is counting one word per egg (one-to-one matching), not skipping a number word.
The story shows a toy pig sliding feet first on a toy slide in the kitchen, but never says that children should go down a playground slide feet first.

'She pointed at a little note. Felix tapped soft... She pointed at a big note. Felix hit hard.' The size of a written note does not show how loud to play; loudness is marked separately (for example p and f).

'The doctor listened to Ruby's neck and back with a soft tool... That is your heart.' Doctors listen to the heart with a stethoscope on the chest; on the back they listen to the lungs, and a stethoscope is not a soft tool.
'They are at the top of my nose!' The nostrils are at the bottom of the nose, and nobody corrects the child.

'He forgot to add the milk!... The pancakes did not puff up. They sat flat' / 'with milk... the pancakes puffed up big'. Milk is not what makes pancakes rise (baking powder does); flour and egg without milk make a thick dough, not flat pancakes.
'He picked up all ten of his hands' worth, one, two, three, four, five.' He has five monkeys, not ten; the count contradicts itself.
The story never says not to put fingers or things into an outlet; Mama just plugs in the nightlight.

'Sarah shared one cookie with Grandma. "We have the same now," said Sarah.' After Grandma gave Sarah two of five cookies and Sarah gave one back, Sarah has 1 and Grandma has 4, not the same. Also 'Nine again... Same number' follows a first count of ten, so the start-anywhere fact is muddled.
'She showed Brielle how to pinch the pencil near the top.' A correct pencil grip pinches the pencil near the point (the sharpened end), not near the top.
'Ben put bread in the toaster. He got it out with a fork.' Putting a metal fork into a toaster is an electric-shock hazard; this unsafe practice is shown as normal.
'Opposites are two different words,' said Sam. Opposites are not just any two different words; they are words that mean things as different as they can be, like big and small.
Audrey wants to write her name and 'She wrote A, U, D, and then a big, happy K.' Audrey is spelled A-U-D-R-E-Y; it has no K.
Of big A and small a: 'They both had the same bump and the same tail!' Capital A and lowercase a have different shapes; they are the same letter but do not look alike.
'Sing the happy birthday song while you scrub' ... 'She finished the song. Then she rinsed.' One Happy Birthday takes about 10 seconds; the CDC guidance is to hum it twice for 20 seconds.
'He watched the pencil marks dry.' Pencil marks are not wet and do not need to dry.

'But the wing was not blue. It was muddy and dark.' A little yellow mixed into blue makes a greenish blue, not muddy dark; also 'The water turned yellow, then clear again' is wrong, rinse water stays tinted.

After lunch at school, the teacher says 'It is dark outside. It is still night.' and 'The moon was up.' Midday rest time is daytime; turning off the lights does not make it night, and turning them on does not make it morning.
'It tastes plain now! Where did the sweet go?' Holding your nose dulls a food's flavor, but the tongue still tastes sweetness, so the strawberry would still taste sweet.
'A little green frog sat by the pond!' ... 'The frog jumped one time, then two times.' Frogs hibernate through winter and are not out hopping in the snow.
'A bird swam in the little birdbath.' Birdbaths are shallow; birds splash and bathe in them, they do not swim in them.
'Arthur rested all morning... His cough was gone.' A cold does not go away after one morning of rest; colds usually last about a week, and rest helps the body recover over that time.

'The water did not feel cold at all' after the warm shower, and the girl who 'skipped the shower' shivers until she showers. Pools ask for a shower for cleanliness; a warm shower does not make pool water feel warmer (it usually feels colder after).

'That's a new shape,' says Ben of the square turned corner-up, and turning it back makes 'the same square' reappear. A square turned so a corner points up is still a square; the story never says so and implies the opposite.

'Mama came in with warm milk... The kittens drank and drank.' Very young kittens should not be given cow's milk (most cats cannot digest it well); young kittens need their mother's milk or kitten formula.
'Why did his hair move? Because his head was attached to his head!' This explanation is wrong; hair moves because it grows from (is attached to) the head, so it moves when the head moves.
'B says bear,' he said. The letter B says the /b/ sound, not the word "bear"; B is for bear.
'"Is it tomorrow now?" Kayden asked. "Yes," said Mom.' The day that was called tomorrow yesterday is today now; it is not tomorrow, so the answer teaches the wrong time word.
